catalog_quote: Stress occurs obligatorily on the first syllable of most stems, on the syllable before a contour except in emphatic sentences and yes-no questions, and on a lexically determined syllable of some polysyllabic loans. (Day 1973:20)

audit.reasoning: Quote check: the two quotations the record actually carries (DiCanio & Bennett preprint p.10; Day 1973:20 as relayed by StressTyp2 lect 589) are both present verbatim in held files at the stated locators, and Bennett 2016 p.495 is confirmed too. The classification (initial, weight-blind, WORD domain with a phrase-final/pre-contour prominence noted separately and loanword exceptions) matches every source opened: StressTyp2 Initial, WALS 14A Initial/15A Fixed, and both Mayanist surveys ('normally on the first syllable of the word or root'). Nothing found suggests the coding is wrong, and the specialist literature as of 2016-2018 still cites only Day 1973 for Popti' stress, so no better stress description is known to exist — hence 'adequate' rather than 'at-risk'. sources.quote: "Phrasally-determined stress: Several languages in the Q'anjob'alan subgroup of Western Mayan have variable stress conditioned by phrasal position: stress is normally on the first syllable of the word or root, but shifts to the final syllable in phrase-final position. Phrasally-conditioned stress is well-documented for Q'anjob'al (5), and its close relatives Akatek and Popti' (Day 1973, England 2001)." (DiCanio & Bennett, Prosody in Mesoamerican Languages, preprint p. 10,)
